prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1008; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a rear-end collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped at a traffic signal. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver of the insured vehicle is listed on the policy and that coverage was in force on the date of loss. Opened a physical damage file and an injury file.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and records the rear impact as described. Requested the photographs taken at the scene for review.

Entry 4: Reviewed scene photographs. They show damage consistent with the reported impact, and the rear bumper and trunk area line up with the position of the vehicles as described. No independent witnesses were identified in the report or by the attorney's office.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspection completed. The damage pattern matches the described impact and there is no indication of prior damage to the vehicle. Estimate issued for repairs.

Entry 6: Received the medical records summary. The reported injury is whiplash, which fits the kind and force of a rear impact of this type. No prior treatment to the neck or upper back appears in the records requested so far, and no earlier injury to that area is known to us.

Entry 7: Recorded a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account of the collision is consistent with the police report and with the earlier first notice of loss.

Entry 8: Follow-up call with the claimant's attorney. The claimant has given the same account in each conversation so far, with no changes to the sequence of events or the vehicles involved.

Entry 9: Physical therapy and follow-up visits have continued for longer than is typical for this type of injury. Requested updated treatment notes and an explanation of the ongoing care plan.

Entry 10: Reviewed the policy history. Nothing in the file suggests that the damage occurred before the coverage period began.

Entry 11: Received the updated treatment records and the treating provider's narrative. The narrative attributes the ongoing symptoms to the collision and describes the course of care in detail. Referred the file for a secondary medical review of the treatment length.

Entry 12: Reserves reviewed and updated to reflect the vehicle repair estimate and the current injury evaluation. File remains open pending the secondary review and further correspondence with counsel.
